decisions_log.decision: Added AC14 test to the existing filter-url-sync.test.tsx rather than creating ChangelogFilteredList.urlparams.test.tsx
decisions_log.rationale: The reviewer approved the previous attempt except for AC14. The test for AC14 naturally belongs alongside the other URL-sync tests in filter-url-sync.test.tsx, which already covers AC1-AC12. Creating a separate file would split related tests without benefit.

decisions_log.decision: AC14 test uses input.value length assertion as the discriminating check, not entry filtering
decisions_log.rationale: No entry title is 200+ chars, so a 200-char substring search would always return 0 results whether truncation happens or not — that comparison is not discriminating. The input.value.length check is: without .slice(0,200), value is 500 chars and the assertion fails; with it, value is exactly 200 chars and the assertion passes. Per DTI-01, this is the correct discriminating input.

deferred_questions.question: node_modules is absent from the working tree so the test suite could not be executed locally. The previous attempt was approved by the reviewer for AC1-AC12, and this revision makes only the two targeted changes (slice bound + AC14 test). If CI is available, it should confirm the full suite passes.

files_changed.summary: Added .slice(0, 200) to the q param at read time, bounding the search input and filter predicate to 200 characters (AC14). Comment added explaining the rationale.

Added AC14 test: constructs a 500-char q value, renders the component, asserts input.value.length === 200 and equals the 200-char prefix. Discriminating because without slice(0,200) the assertion fails.

self_assessment.notes: Revision addressed exactly the two items the reviewer named: (1) .slice(0, 200) applied to qParam at read time in ChangelogFilteredList.tsx, and (2) an AC14-named test added to filter-url-sync.test.tsx. No other files were touched. AC11 (Back-button behaviour) has no automated test; this is inherent to the browser history API and cannot be tested in jsdom — noted in the previous implementation's deferred_questions and still stands.
